summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of refractory ileocolonic Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileosigmoid anastomosis, was admitted with a two-day history of severe colicky right upper abdominal pain, nausea, and reduced bowel frequency. He had recently tapered prednisone from 10 mg to 5 mg daily and was on Tysabri therapy. Initial imaging showed no obstruction or free air. A CT scan revealed worsening inflammation at the rectosigmoid junction with a focal intramural phlegmon and mild proximal bowel dilation, but no abscess or perforation. Workup for nephrolithiasis, infection, and DVT was negative. MRI of the lumbar spine showed stable degenerative changes. He was treated with IV solumedrol and hydrocortisone enemas, then transitioned to oral prednisone. His pain improved, white count normalized, and he was discharged home on a prednisone taper, rectal steroids, and continued Tysabri with follow-up planned with gastroenterology.
problems: Carbuncle and furuncle of unspecified site
